correctness.rationale: Exact elimination of typewise endemic balances yields a strictly decreasing scalar equation with a unique positive root. For each fixed positive root argument the response kernel is strictly convex in reciprocal waning rate, so standard convex order and implicit monotonicity yield the full inequality; derivative arguments give strict two-type monotonicity for every split. The second-order coefficient follows from the implicit-function theorem and was reconstructed independently. Standalone 5,109 assertion checker passed. All positivity, normalization and epidemic threshold requirements are specified; the proof is analytical and independent of finite experiments.

originality.rationale: The closest 2023/2024 primary SIRS treatment restricts the epidemic burden monotonicity proof to \(p\geq 1/2\) and explicitly leaves \(p<1/2\) to simulation. The full final article, its original appendices, another within-person waning comparison, a general vaccine-interval convex-order paper, relevant published mathematical findings and recoverable previous claims were compared by implications. No covering theorem for the missing parameter case or finite-type convex-order extension was identified. Existing SIRS equilibrium uniqueness and Jensen theory are acknowledged prior tools; publication-priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: No negative-search conclusion proves publication priority; an unlocated general convex-order theorem for endemic equilibria may subsume the result.
The conclusion does not apply to vaccine schedules or partial (gradual) immunity; those distinct models have their own order questions.
